text:
Braden Schneider has two assists in 21 games and no goals, and Blue Seat Blogs called him a mystery for the Rangers while BVM Sports asked whether it's time to move on. With Sean Durzi out, though, he's moved in beside Marcus Pettersson, and his ice time is up to more than 20 minutes a night.

The physical game is intact, 52 hits and 28 blocks, but the offense isn't there. He has 31 shots and 0.96 expected goals, and the Rangers take 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a bit below their team rate, with only 46% of the shot attempts. Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 1% of defensemen for creating offense last season and noted his results ran ahead of his chances.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking names the specific weakness: only 30% of his exits keep possession, so watch for clears off the glass when the forecheck comes. The 2020 first-round pick is 25 and has 389 games in New York, so this is who he is more than who he might become. Our talent range has him around 15 points. The bigger minutes are a test.
